items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: I went to a gentleman named Art -- Mr. Art Beam. Mr. Art Beam was a musician, and he sold instruments... Mr. Beam told me that he couldn't teach me because I was colored

ctx.x: And by 1963 -- I mean 1923 we had finished paying for the house, and we had enough money to pay down -- to have carpenters come in and to move that house a little bit away from the street and add two more rooms to it. And I sacrificed every penny that I made to do this.

In the meantime I was falling in love -- had fallen in love with music. Come April in 1923, I told my dad I wanted to buy a saxophone. My dad says, "Well, if you want to buy a saxophone, Hayes, then go ahead. It's pretty expensive but if you think you can make it, go ahead. I'll help you." I went to a gentleman named Art -- Mr. Art Beam. Mr. Art Beam was a musician, and he sold instruments. And I had to go to see my horn and go on the back porch. He didn't invite me into his
house. I had to go in the back of the back porch to see this horn.
